scene.label: Interactive 3D lesson network for the identity foundation: SBD-DC01 and SBD-DC02 on VLAN 10, the offline root CA, the issuing CA and publication host on VLAN 30, the DHCP server for VLAN 80, and the administration seats on VLAN 60, joined through the core.
scene.completeCaption: Both domain controllers hold the sbd.test directory and DNS and keep the domain on time; they are measured against the STIG and hardened with Group Policy. The two-tier PKI issues their certificates, DHCP serves VLAN 80 with secure DNS updates, and Tier 0 is administered only from its own seats. Every later course builds on this foundation.

nodes.name: SBD-DC01
nodes.title: SBD-DC01 · 10.0.10.10
nodes.description: The first domain controller, promoted in chapter 2 to create the sbd.test forest. It holds the directory, DNS and the five operations master roles; as PDC emulator it is the time source for the whole network. Its default gateway is the core's VLAN 10 address, 10.0.10.1.

nodes.name: SBD-DC02
nodes.title: SBD-DC02 · 10.0.10.11
nodes.description: The second writable domain controller, added in chapter 3 so the directory has two service points. It holds its own copy of the directory and DNS, replicates with SBD-DC01 in both directions, and keeps the domain available while either controller is down.

nodes.name: TEST CLIENT
nodes.title: Test client · where lookups and leases are proven
nodes.description: Where the build is tested from. In parts 2 and 3 it stands for any domain member that lists both controllers for DNS and follows the domain time; part 7 makes it the disposable VLAN 80 client, outside the domain, that proves the DHCP relay, the options and secure name registration.

nodes.name: SBD-ROOTCA01
nodes.title: SBD-ROOTCA01 · offline, no network address
nodes.description: The trust anchor: a standalone root CA in a workgroup with no network path, configured in lesson 2. It signs the issuing CA’s certificate at the ceremony and publishes a base CRL every 26 weeks; everything crossing its boundary travels on approved removable media.

nodes.name: SBD-SUBCA01
nodes.title: SBD-SUBCA01 · 10.0.30.20
nodes.description: The enterprise issuing CA, joined to sbd.test on VLAN 30. It creates its request in lesson 29, starts with its signed certificate in lesson 31, writes its CRLs to pki.sbd.test, and publishes only the three templates from lesson 9.

nodes.name: SBD-PKI-MGMT01
nodes.title: SBD-PKI-MGMT01 · 10.0.30.30
nodes.description: A hardened member server on VLAN 30 with two jobs in this part: from lesson 32 it hosts the pki.sbd.test publication site over plain HTTP, and from lesson 34 it is the only seat for certificate template administration. In lesson 36 it is also the pilot that autoenrolls a computer certificate.

nodes.name: SBD-DHCP01
nodes.title: SBD-DHCP01 · 10.0.20.10
nodes.description: Built in lesson 38 on VLAN 20 as a member server in the Servers OU, run at its console by SBD Tier 1 Admins. It leases the VLAN 80 pool through the core’s relay (F04), registers client names as svc-dhcp-dns with name protection, and keeps its audit-log copies on its second volume; course 1.12 backs it up.

nodes.name: AdminJumpBox01
nodes.title: AdminJumpBox01 · 10.0.60.10
nodes.description: The Tier 0 seat in the Admin Servers OU. Tier 0 accounts manage the domain controllers, SBD-SUBCA01, and SBD-PKI-MGMT01 from here (rule A01), and it is the only seat allowed to reach the core router’s management on VLAN 100. From lesson 46 it also holds SCC, STIG Viewer, and the Tier 0 evidence.

nodes.name: SBD-ADMIN-SRV01
nodes.title: SBD-ADMIN-SRV01 · 10.0.60.20
nodes.description: The Tier 1 seat in the Admin Servers OU, for member-server administration such as SBD-DHCP01 (rule A02). It also hosts the SBD-ADMIN-PC01 virtual machine, so three seats run on two machines, and the audit custodian’s separate accounts and sessions start here too. From lesson 46 it holds the Tier 1 copy of the assessment tools.

nodes.name: SBD-ADMIN-PC01
nodes.title: SBD-ADMIN-PC01 · 10.0.60.30
nodes.description: The Tier 2 seat: a Windows client virtual machine on SBD-ADMIN-SRV01, in the Admin Workstations OU, for endpoint administration (rule A03). Tier 2 accounts sign in only inside it, never on its host, and Tier 0, Tier 1, and audit custodian accounts are refused there. In this part it manages the VLAN 80 test client and, from lesson 46, holds its own SCC copy and first baseline; the fleet arrives in course 1.6.

flows.label: Directory, DNS and domain time served to the network
A second service point for the segment
Time from the PDC emulator · UDP 123
Hashed results to the evidence folder · SMB 445
Reports and rescan results to SBD-DC01’s evidence folder · SMB 445
Ceremony media · request in, public artifacts out
Issuing CA CRL publication · on schedule
Root certificate and CRL · hand-carried media
DHCP lease through the core relay (F04)
Secure dynamic DNS update as svc-dhcp-dns (F01)
Zone replication of the client records

chapters.network: Nothing is built yet. VLAN 10 is reserved for the two domain controllers, and the design record decides what they will hold.
Both controllers are planned on VLAN 10, the domain controllers' own segment. The platform and network exist, but domain services have not been built yet.
DC01 now hosts the sbd.test domain. DC02 is still planned; no replication relationship is shown yet.
Both controllers serve the sbd.test domain. The animated relationship represents directory replication, not a measured packet capture.

Follow a health check from the administration viewpoint to either controller, and switch the target to check the other. The arc between the controllers is the replication you confirm in both directions.
Both controllers are built and verified for this part. Continue into the full network to see the services that later lessons can add.

Both controllers run DNS on VLAN 10. The paths from the domain member to each controller are rule F01, TCP and UDP 53: a member has to find a controller before any Kerberos, LDAP, or Group Policy traffic can start.

The arc between the controllers is Active Directory replication carrying the sbd.test and 10.0.10.in-addr.arpa zone data, not a zone transfer. No member traffic is shown while the zones are configured.
Records created on one controller reach the other through directory replication. The animation represents that relationship, not a measured packet capture.

Follow lookups from the domain member to each controller, and to the remaining one during the failover test. Replication between the controllers stays in view because DCDiag and the replication summary check it.
Every path the course built is shown: lookups to both controllers and replication between them. Work through them one layer at a time when a name fails to resolve.
Both controllers are live on VLAN 10. The paths from a domain member to each controller are rule F09, UDP 123, which this plan confirms; SBD-DC02's own time requests to SBD-DC01 stay inside VLAN 10.

SBD-DC01 serves time from its own clock, with nothing above it, and SBD-DC02 takes its time from it over UDP 123 inside VLAN 10. The configuration and the reference check happen at the controllers' consoles; no member path is shown in this lesson.

SBD-DC02 takes time from the PDC emulator, and the domain member from either controller, all on UDP 123 under rule F09. The member stands for every Windows member and for the Linux servers later courses build with this chrony file.

Checks run from the controllers' consoles and from the member: w32tm /monitor queries both controllers, and the member samples its offset from SBD-DC01. The whole hierarchy stays in view because every measurement is taken along it.
Every time path the course built is shown: SBD-DC02 from the PDC emulator, the member from either controller, and the checks at the consoles. Work along them from the symptom to the clock that broke.
Both controllers are live on VLAN 10 and unchanged. From each VM console you read the operating system, roles and forest to record which STIGs apply; nothing is installed yet.

Nothing crosses the network in this lesson: the content arrives on approved removable media at each controller’s console. SCC is installed on both controllers and STIG Viewer on SBD-DC01; the GPO package and the Windows client content wait, hashed, in C:\Staging\DISA.

SCC scans each controller locally from its console. SBD-DC02’s hashed results are copied to the evidence folder on SBD-DC01 over SMB inside VLAN 10, and no DISA policy has been imported yet: this is the before picture.

STIG Viewer runs at SBD-DC01’s console, with both controllers’ results already in its evidence folder. The manual checks are answered by examining each controller and the sbd.test directory they share.

The findings record and the handoff are written at SBD-DC01’s console into C:\Evidence\baseline. Both controllers wait unchanged for part 5, which imports the staged GPOs and rescans with the same versions.
Both controllers are live on VLAN 10. The new OUs are directory objects, so they replicate between SBD-DC01 and SBD-DC02; the controllers themselves stay in the built-in Domain Controllers OU.

Both controllers on VLAN 10 still apply only the two default policies. The central store created on SBD-DC01 is a SYSVOL folder, so DFS Replication carries it to SBD-DC02, just as directory replication carries each GPO’s Active Directory half.

The central store and the imported GPOs live in SYSVOL and replicate between SBD-DC01 and SBD-DC02. The domain controller policy links to the Domain Controllers OU, so both controllers apply it; the member-server policy waits on the Servers OU for the systems later courses build.

The scans return to both controllers on VLAN 10, now with the DISA policies applied. Each controller is rescanned locally at its console and compared with its own baseline; SBD-DC02’s hashed results are carried to SBD-DC01.

The hardened controllers stay on VLAN 10. The GPO reports and link export are hashed into the evidence folder on SBD-DC01, course 1.12 backs the GPOs up, and the next scan waits for the DISA quarter or part 6’s change.

Nothing is built yet. SBD-ROOTCA01 is planned with no network connection, and SBD-SUBCA01 and SBD-PKI-MGMT01 are planned on VLAN 30. SBD-DC01 already provides the domain and DNS the issuing CA will depend on.
SBD-ROOTCA01 is now a standalone root CA in the offline vault, drawn in amber with no cable to the core. Nothing travels to or from it yet; SBD-SUBCA01 and SBD-PKI-MGMT01 are still planned.

SBD-SUBCA01 joins VLAN 30 at 10.0.30.20 as an enterprise subordinate CA, waiting for its certificate. Its request file carries only the public key and goes to the media custodian, not across the network.

The request travels to SBD-ROOTCA01 on approved removable media, and the signed subordinate certificate, root certificate, and current root CRL travel back the same way. The amber path is carried by hand; there is no network link to the root.

SBD-SUBCA01 is now a running issuing CA on VLAN 30, and SBD-DC01 carries the Group Policy that delivers the approved root to domain clients. SBD-PKI-MGMT01 is still planned, so the pki.sbd.test URLs have nowhere to answer yet.
SBD-PKI-MGMT01 comes online at 10.0.30.30 and answers for pki.sbd.test on HTTP TCP 80. SBD-DC01, outside VLAN 30, resolves the name and reaches the site across the core under rule F18.

Trust data now reaches pki.sbd.test: the issuing CA writes its CRLs to the site on schedule, and the root’s certificate and CRL arrive by hand-carried media. SBD-DC01 fetches each AIA and CDP URL over HTTP TCP 80.

SBD-PKI-MGMT01 is now also the template administration seat. Template work goes from it to the directory on SBD-DC01, where templates live as objects; the issuing CA’s console stays for CA operations.
Templates are configured from SBD-PKI-MGMT01 and stored in the directory on SBD-DC01, and SBD-SUBCA01 now publishes exactly the three planned templates. Nothing has enrolled yet.

Both domain controllers autoenroll from SBD-SUBCA01 across the core, and the pilot, SBD-PKI-MGMT01, inside VLAN 30. SBD-DC01 validates against pki.sbd.test over HTTP TCP 80, the issuing CA publishes its updated CRL to the site, and the root’s replacement CRLs keep arriving through scheduled, hand-carried ceremonies.
Nothing is built yet. SBD-DC01 and SBD-DC02 run from part 1; SBD-DHCP01 and the VLAN 80 test client exist only in the plan, and the core’s relay is already part of the network.
SBD-DHCP01 on VLAN 20 checks its authorization in the directory and leases an address to the VLAN 80 test client through the core relay (F04). No client name is registered yet.
SBD-DHCP01 now registers the test client’s A, PTR, and DHCID records with the domain controllers as svc-dhcp-dns, and the records replicate between SBD-DC01 and SBD-DC02.
The lease path from lesson 38 stays live while SBD-DHCP01 keeps its audit trail on its second volume. No new network path is added.
The test client renews through the core relay and its records answer from both controllers. The refused takeover shows up in SBD-DHCP01’s logs, not as a new path.
Nothing new is built yet. SBD-DC01, SBD-SUBCA01, and part 7’s SBD-DHCP01 run from earlier courses; the three VLAN 60 seats exist only in the plan.

The three administration seats are online in VLAN 60. Management reaches out from them, AdminJumpBox01 to the domain controllers (A01) and SBD-ADMIN-SRV01 to SBD-DHCP01 (A02), and nothing initiates toward them.
The Tier 0 servers have their own OU. AdminJumpBox01 still manages SBD-SUBCA01 after the move, while the Servers and Workstations OUs now refuse Tier 0 sign-ins.

Each tier’s path runs from its own seat: A01 to the domain controller and SBD-SUBCA01, A02 to SBD-DHCP01, A03 to the test client. Part 7’s lease runs again under the full rule set; the refused attempts show up in logs, not as paths.

All three seats are baselined and the changed systems rescanned, with the assessment tools now on the seats. The finished management plane stays in view: each seat reaches only its own tier, ready for course 1.2.
